name: NJ-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans R+14, a steep structural advantage for Republicans
Chris Smith has held the seat since 1981, a powerful incumbency edge
Smith has raised roughly seven times more than Rachel Peace and holds a large cash-on-hand lead
Prediction markets price Smith near 98% to win
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: the district's R+14 lean, Smith's four-decade incumbency, a lopsided fundraising gap, and market pricing near 98% Republican, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting competitiveness.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or fresh polling showing a far tighter race would be the main reason to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New Jersey's 4th District leans firmly Republican, and Chris Smith has represented it since 1981, making him one of the longest-serving members of the House. No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, campaign resources, and market pricing. Prediction markets put Smith's chances near 98%, and his campaign has raised roughly seven times more than Democratic challenger Rachel Peace, with a wide cash-on-hand advantage heading into the fall.

Peace enters the general election with limited funds and minimal outside support, and no major expert ratings flag the district as competitive. A modestly favorable national environment for Republicans adds to the structural headwind. Barring an unexpected development, Smith is positioned for another term, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
